thread:
Ava: quick thread — i'm proposing a TTL-based PII exemption for route-level debug logs. goal: let short-lived requests (eg 30s TTL) opt into less-aggressive redaction while still being audited. thoughts? :eyes:
Dev: can you sketch the use case? when would we flip the exemption at runtime vs config?
Ava: main use case = debugging real-time user flows where the request lifecycle is < TTL (eg websocket handshake, streaming init). ops want higher-fidelity traces for 30s window to speed triage. not for long-term retention.
Priya: strong :lock: from compliance — exemptions need explicit consent and an audit trail. TTL doesn't equal consent. how do you prove user consent for a given request?
Ava: agreed. plan: require either (1) explicit consent token header `X-PII-CONSENT` signed by our auth service, or (2) route-level policy that is limited to internal-only routes. no global on/off.
Mike L: implementation idea: add a route config block + runtime header check. example config snippet: ```yaml
routes:
  - path: /connect/*
    debug_exemptions:
      enabled: true
      ttl_ms: 30000
      require_consent: true
      sample_rate: 0.01
```
Sam: alternative that might satisfy compliance: never store raw PII, only store hashes derived with per-customer KMS key + salted nonce that rotates. then exemptions let us capture hashed values for debugging but not raw. tradeoff: harder to read in logs.
Priya: hashing helps but is not equivalent to consent. we need: who authorized, why, and short retention. add an audit entry with request id + actor. Also lock down access via console role.
Marco: console UX question — product support wants an "enable debug for route X for 1h" button that does the right backend dance (consent check, audit entry, auto-expire). can we expose that without creating a footgun?
Ava: propose a safe workflow: support clicks button -> generates a signed `X-PII-CONSENT` token scoped to route + time-window -> token stored in audit log with actor -> runtime honors token. UI must show last-used tokens and require reason text.
Dev: for rollout, we should default to off and ship a canary where exemptions only work for internal orgs. also need metrics: how often tokens issued, sample sizes, and any retractions.
Mike L: on sampling: i think combine TTL exemption with a floor sample rate (eg 0.1%) to avoid complete blindspots. also surface token issuance in per-route telemetry dashboard.
Priya: require KMS-backed signing for consent tokens. no plain JWTs. audit retention policy: tokens + linked logs kept for 90 days, then scrubbed.
Sam: small ops caveat — some routes stream and exceed TTL. need clear semantics: TTL applies to request initiation time, not total duration. otherwise we get partial redaction mid-stream.
Ava: good catch. define TTL semantics in the config doc: `ttl_ms` is max time from request start to allow exempt capture. after that we fall back to redacted mode.
Marco: UX: show a yellow banner on route page when active exemptions exist, plus a one-click revoke. keep permission scope to Support+SRE.
sre-bot: deploy by canary to infra/region-eu scheduled at 03:00 UTC. tickets: #INF-4217, #SEC-889.
Compliance: summary from our side: acceptable only if (a) signed consent token OR (b) internal-only route + audit trail + KMS signing + 90d retention + explicit revoke. also we need a threat model doc before GA.
Ava: thanks — i'll draft RFC with config schemas, token format (KMS-signed), console flows, and canary plan. will ping for review. :thumbsup:
Dev: ping me on the RFC, i'll add sampling math and telemetry hooks.
Mike L: i'll prototype the runtime header check and fallback logic (ttl vs duration).
Priya: i'll coordinate on threat model and legal signoff.
Ava: plan to post RFC tomorrow AM.
Sam: one last note — consider a dev-only shim that prints hashed PII in staging for faster dev loops. must be gated.
Ava: noted. thanks everyone.
